description: KerfScript is a programming language for laser cutting, like OpenSCAD for flat parts. Write a part once as code, change a number, and get a new cut file. Cut, score and engrave layers, kerf compensation, finger joints, living hinges, parts and sheets are built in. It is also a JavaScript and WebAssembly library for building generators that take a few settings and return SVG or DXF files ready to cut.
rules: KerfScript uses OpenSCAD syntax but makes 2D parts only. cube, sphere, cylinder, polyhedron, linear_extrude, rotate_extrude, projection, minkowski, resize, color, import, surface and render are errors.
Lengths are millimetres and angles are degrees. The x axis points right and the y axis up. rect() starts at [0, 0] unless center = true.
Assignments take effect in order, unlike OpenSCAD: a value assigned later does not change geometry made earlier.
Choose the operation with cut(), score(), engrave(), guide() or layer(), not color(). Shapes go on the cut layer by default.
Name pieces with part("name", qty = n). Put score() and engrave() inside a part, not around it.
Set $kerf and $thickness in millimetres for the material, or per material with material(thickness = ..., kerf = ...). Apply kerf compensation in KerfScript or in the laser software, never both.
A comment after an assignment makes it a setting: width = 80; // [40:5:200] is a slider from 40 to 200 in steps of 5.
Load standard library modules with use, for example use <kerf/box> for box().
Type errors stop evaluation with an error instead of producing undef.
Fonts come from the application or the CLI, not from system fonts.
In JavaScript, parameters(source) reads a design's settings, and render(source, { params }) returns sheets (each with svg and dxf), parts and warnings.
Run programs you did not write in a web worker with a timeout, and limit the resolve callback to the libraries you intend to expose.
